doc.title: Bill Easley interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 1, 2021

title: Broadway career, Black and Blue and gratitude
summary: His Broadway shows were jazz-themed and he engaged fully with the show; he lives in truth, gratitude and happiness.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Did you have something you did when you were in the pit to help keep focused when you had 84 measures of rest and then you had to come in? Because it’s been my observation that, you know when you play a show over and over and over you have these long periods of not playing that your mind can start going out.

You know what? That’s a brilliant point. And my experience is totally — because that’s the norm. See that’s the norm. It’s going to the assembly line. You have to realize I had a very, very unique Broadway career. In other words I went to “Sophisticated Ladies” to a show called “Black and Blue” you know which was filled with jazz all-stars. I did “Jelly’s Last Jam” where the clarinet was just all throughout the whole thing. And most of my shows have not been your typical Broadway shows, you see they’ve been jazz- themed shows. And most of my chairs have been with me in mind you see. I’ve been hired for, you know, “Get Bill Easley” because that’s what Bill Easley does. You know. And I bet my experience is not typical. If I’m playing a Broadway show, or anything that I’m playing, I was not involved with the show or the music [gap] is in my face. I’m involved with the whole experience. So no, my norm is not to okay play this and then pick up a book and read a chapter of this. No. If I go to work I’m there to work, and I’m involved with all, not just my part but everything going around me and during — the actors and the singers. In other words I used to go to work every night in “Black and Blue,” oh is Sir Roland Hanna going to play tonight. You understand? What is he going to play tonight? You know. And so that, I hate to brag but not many people have had that kind of experience you see.
It’s okay with me if you brag.

No, you know, because you’ll turn me off. Look, listen man, I can’t help but to brag because I’ve had the best life and, when you talk about them cats that are mad all the time and so and so, I’ve never been one of those guys. You know I live in three states: the truth, the state of gratitude, and the state of happiness. And everything else is a waste of my time see. And I’m still living that way.
Past, present and future all exist simultaneously.
